terra.problem: John 7:14 places Jesus in the temple courts in the middle of the feast; it does not establish that He is there on the last day when He speaks in this passage.
John 7:14 places Jesus in the temple courts in the middle of the feast, but it does not say that He and the crowd are standing there on the last day.
Elijah is identified as a prophet without a reference for that fact from outside the passage.
The passage does not record anyone saying Elijah, but it does not establish that nobody in the crowd said it.
The description of Jeremiah as a prophet who wrote down warnings is an outside Bible fact without a reference.
The passage does not record anyone saying Jeremiah, but it does not establish that nobody in the crowd said it.
The passage says some wanted to seize Jesus; it does not say a lot of people had a plan.
The passage does not say the crowds at the feast were big.
Calling the Pharisees' words harsh adds a comment to the text's harsh statement about the crowd. Papa also comments on how he is telling the text.
Saying a blessing would be friendlier and wishing that were what the Pharisees said adds his own comment to their harsh statement about the crowd.
Calling the Pharisees' statement a sharp thing to say adds his own comment to the text's harsh statement about the crowd.
The claim that the Sabbath comes up with Jesus a lot refers to events outside this passage without a reference.
